title: Layout Data Model File
description: ADR 0008 rev 4 on ADR 0009, reshaped by ADR 0011 and ADR 0012. One file holds one layout: every entity and row holds three maps, given (what a person stated as fields, as drawn), relations (what a person stated as connections, each the name it reaches) and derived (what the rules compute, stamped by provenance.rules). Readers take meaning from derived, then relations, then given. Collections, identities (map keys, a row's name and id) and geometry stay outside the maps. Absent is absent. Nothing here names a sheet, a net, a reference or a KiCad symbol unit. Version 3.1.0 is a working schema, reshaped in place (2026-10-27; v3.1.0-migration.md).

name.description: An entity's own name within its scope: case preserved, compared case-folded, never a colon or a slash, no leading or trailing space, no line break or tab.

qualifiedName.description: A reference to an entity of a namespace other than the layout: an interlocking or an OfficeUnit, a colon, the entity's name (Luchessa:783, SPCoast South:12). Always this form (ADR 0008 §4.5; three-maps D19).

layoutName.description: A reference to an entity of the layout scope (an interlocking, office unit, transport, code line, I/O encoding or processor): its bare name.

route.description: A device pin's binding: bus owner, address on that bus, driver pin. Three segments: a processor's bus, processor/address/pin (Sargent/0x20/B1). Four: a CMRInet Node's bus, transport/UA/IB.n or OB.n/pin (CMRInet/30/OB.7/D). The segment count tells the owner's kind (ADR 0009 §3.3, §3.5).

namedMap.description: A dictionary keyed by entity name.

given.description: Every field a person stated on the entity, keyed as drawn, every value a string as KiCad states it (ADR 0011 §2). Left out: KiCad's housekeeping (Reference, Value, Footprint, Datasheet, Description, Sheetname, Sheetfile, ki_*), Role (it picks the collection), the library's Pin.* contract, the key field, and any empty field. Which keys apply is reference data, not this schema's; a reader that wants a number or a list parses the string.

relations.description: Every connection a person stated, each written as the name it reaches (ADR 0011 §2): a layout name, a qualified name, a port, a route, or a list of them; a device's bindings are a map from function to route. An entity's definition names the relations it may hold.

derived.description: What the rules compute from given and relations, by a conforming derivation stamped in provenance.rules (ADR 0011 §3); never a copy of a stated value. An entity's definition names the keys it may hold.

rowId.description: A track row's stable opaque identity (three-maps D10): by default the KiCad per-instance UUID of its symbol. Unique in the file; never a name.

portRef.description: A switch's track port, a track circuit marker's TC, or a pin of a named track symbol, by qualified name: the switch, marker or symbol, a dot, and the pin as the model names it (a switch's C, N or R, a derail's C or R; a marker's TC; an industry's EoT): Luchessa:783.R, Luchessa:1SAT.TC, Luchessa:Gilroy Industry.EoT.

rowPortRef.description: A pin of an unnamed track row, by the row's id, a dot and its side (approach, governed, A, B, track, CTC, DARK, EoT).

portRefs.description: Every other track pin a track pin's wire reaches, sorted and without repeats (three-maps D5; the owner, 2026-10-27): a switch port, a track circuit marker's TC or a named track row's side by qualified name, an unnamed track row's side by the row's id. Never a pin of the same symbol; symmetric: the pin named here names this one back.

layout.description: The layout and its layout-scope entities. Its name is the Railroad symbol's Name; given holds the Railroad symbol's other fields (Railroad, Region, Era, Rulebook, by which reference data is looked up, ADR 0012 §6).

transport.description: A mechanism (ADR 0009 §3.4): a broker, a serial port and baud, DC pulses. One entity however many times it is placed; given merged over its placements (Kind, Broker, Port, Baud). Each placement's Processor wire is an anchor.

anchors.description: The processors on which an instance of this transport is drawn and wired.

nodes.description: CMRInet Nodes on this line, keyed by UA (their Address); the container is the relation (three-maps D12).

cmrinetNode.description: A CMRInet Node: a driver on the line that provides a bus for its bits (ADR 0009 §3.5). given holds IC, NodeType, InputBytes and OutputBytes as drawn; the KiCad importer checks the declared bytes cover the bits used.

bits.description: The bits in use, keyed IB.n or OB.n (computed from the Bit field and its pin's direction); each is a driver with one pin D.

encodingInstance.description: An encoding riding a transport instance (ADR 0009 §3.4): a code line (codelines{}) or remote I/O (ioEncodings{}). given holds Kind (AAR, USS506, BITS, JMRI, CMRI) and its fields with macros expanded (Topic, Version, Chart).

processor.description: The anchor of the transport placement this encoding is wired to (three-maps D7).

What runs a FieldUnit's or OfficeUnit's logic and anchors its connections (ADR 0009 §3.3). given (Kind, Board) merged over its placements. Its drivers are keyed by their address on its bus; the container is the relation.

driver.description: A driver on a bus, keyed by its Address, or for an encoded driver (a JMRI object) by Kind.name of the device it serves unless an Address is drawn (ADR 0005 S4, R11; three-maps D11). given holds IC, Kind and its fields (frequency_hz, Bit, Node, ...).

interlocking.description: An interlocking, the namespace of its houses, appliances, track and devices. Its FieldUnit runs on relations.processor (three-maps D14).

codeline.description: The one code line this FieldUnit attaches to, by its Codeline wire (ADR 0009 §3.8).

processor.description: The processor that runs its FieldUnit, by its Processor wire.

appliances.description: The trackplan's named things by name (ADR 0010 §4.1).

house.description: An instrument house at a control point, keyed by its CP Name; on a US&S 506 line it is a field station, addressed by its column (derived, not written).

maintainerCall.description: The maintainer call on its MC wire.

codeline.description: The code line on its Codeline wire, where drawn.

device.description: One row of devices[]: one device instance, without identity (ADR 0008 §4.5), so its Name lands in given. given holds Appliance, Style (as drawn, a comma list), Head, Address, Invert, IndicationToken and its fields.

bindings.description: Each device pin's wire to a driver pin: function (the pin, polarity marks removed) to route.

column.description: The OfficeUnit column a panel device sits in, qualified by its OfficeUnit (SPCoast South:12).

interlocking.description: The interlocking a panel device in no column belongs to, stated only by the sheet hierarchy (three-maps D6).

mast.description: A head device's mast, by its IND wire.

serves.description: The appliance this device serves (given.Name in its scope); for a head device, its mast.

shows.description: The indications a lamp shows, OR'd: its IndicationToken resolved in its scope.

officeUnit.description: An OfficeUnit (never machine): given Style, the processor that runs it, its columns and its panel devices.

column.description: A logical column tied to a control point (owner's ruling 2026-10-23), keyed by its Column number. given."CP Name" names its house.

interlocking.description: Its interlocking where only the sheet hierarchy states it (no CP Name; three-maps D6).

provenance.description: A property of the file about the whole layout and nothing below it: what wrote this file, the rules version its derived maps were computed by, and the one source it was imported from, the KiCad project.

path.description: The project file, relative to its repository.

rules.description: The derivation rules' semantic version that produced every derived map (ADR 0011 §3, ADR 0012 §7); present exactly when derived is.

polyline.description: Ordered vertices, SVG points syntax: 'x,y x,y ...'. A string because a JSON list is sorted by the canonical form.

glyphKey.description: The drawing's own name for a glyph: library and symbol, 'Railroad-Trackplan:Switch_Lock'. The library's version is in provenance.

placement.description: Where a glyph sits: its anchor (the glyph's origin, which is its bottom-left pin) on the page, its turn (degrees, counter-clockwise as seen on the page, 0/90/180/270) and its mirror (x: top for bottom; y: left for right), applied mirror first, then turn, then translate; and which glyph.

heads.description: A mast's heads by letter: a head cannot exist alone (view §4).

track.description: One drawn run of track. points is geometry's own; derived.circuit the circuit it carries (absent for dark track); relations.from and .to what each end meets: a switch port or a named track row's pin by name (Luchessa:783.R), an unnamed track row's pin by the row's id and side (three-maps D5, D10). An end at a junction is absent.

marker.description: A track row's placement (a joint, END CTC, NextCP, an industry, a policy sign): the row it places, by id (three-maps D10), and its placement and glyph. It copies no fact of the row.

stroke.description: KiCad's stroke, written only where it is not the default: a width in millimetres (KiCad's 0 means 'the default, which depends on context' and is not written), a dash type other than solid.

fill.description: KiCad's fill, written only where there is one: outline (the stroke colour), background (the sheet's body colour) or a colour of its own.

primitive.description: One drawn element of a glyph, in the glyph's frame: millimetres, x right, y down, the anchor pin at 0,0.

oneOf.description: A circular arc through three points, as KiCad states it.
An axis-aligned rectangle by two opposite corners.
Fixed text that is part of the picture (the H of a hand-thrown switch). A field shown through the symbol is not a primitive: the Layout Data Model File carries the field.

glyph.description: One picture, stated once: its ports (every pin, by name, in the glyph's frame; the anchor pin is 0,0) and its shape. The shape is a list and the canonical form sorts it: drawing order is not a fact.

glyphs.description: layout.glyphs: every glyph any interlocking's geometry names, by glyph key; nothing the layout does not draw.

geometry.description: interlockings.<name>.geometry: an independent section whose one contract with the rest of the file is identity (three-maps D10). Placements are keyed by railroad name, markers name their track row by id, runs name what their ends meet.

mileposts.description: Milepost anchors by milepost (ADR 0004 D7: the Value is the milepost, so it is the marker's name). Luchessa draws two; Sargent none.

appliance.description: A named thing on the trackplan (ADR 0010 §4.1, by Role APPLIANCE), keyed by its Name: given.Appliance is switch (Style derail for a derail), mast, track_circuit, lamp or contact. A reference to another interlocking's appliance is not an appliance of this one.

TC.description: A track circuit marker's TC pin.

house.description: A maintainer call's house, by its MC wire (three-maps D8).

controlPoint.description: The house (control point) the appliance belongs to: its own given.CP; else the one house of its interlocking; else the house its chain of relations reaches.

osCircuit.description: The circuit a switch's or derail's track carries: its marker's name, or else the switch's given.TC. Absent on dark track.

members.description: A virtual track circuit's member circuits, its IndicationToken resolved.

trackSymbol.description: A track row (a joint, an end, a policy sign): its id, its name where it has one (an industry), given (Kind as the libraries spell it, CP, Direction, Interlocking), each side's wire as relations.<side> and each side's circuit as derived.circuits.<side>. Sides are named for what they do (ADR 0012 §8): a signal joint's approach and governed; a policy sign's and a NextCP's track; a plain joint's A and B; CTC, DARK, EoT as drawn.

name.description: The row's name where it has one (an industry).

mast.description: A signal joint's mast, by its SIGNAL wire.

additionalProperties.description: Every other track pin this side's wire reaches: switch ports, markers' TC and named rows' sides by name, unnamed rows' sides by id (three-maps D5).

circuits.description: The circuit at each side; a side on dark track is absent.

controlPoint.description: A signal joint's control point: its given.CP, or its mast's, or the interlocking's one house.

trackplan.description: The interlocking's track as the netlist states it, by circuit, port and row id, never by coordinate (ADR 0010 C6). A circuit is the track between joints and ends, joined through a switch's or derail's ports; dark track has no circuit.

joints.description: IRJ and IRJ_SIGNAL: insulated joints, each between the circuits on its two sides; a signal joint's governed side is where the route it protects begins.

ends.description: END_CTC, NEXT_CP, BUMPER, INDUSTRY: where the drawn track ends, and what lies beyond.

policies.description: The policy signs (RULE_105, RULE_251, RULE_261, RULE_93) with their Direction, on the circuit at their pin.

links.description: Switch ports that meet with no joint or end between them (Luchessa:795.R and Luchessa:795D.R), with the circuit there: computed from the ports' relations.

head.description: A head of a mast, keyed by its letter: an entity nested under its mast (three-maps D9). given holds its Appliance and Style.

link.description: Switch ports that meet with no joint or end between them (Luchessa:795.R and Luchessa:795D.R), with the circuit there: computed from the ports' relations.
